Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia and Urinary Retention

three-stage history · retention, infection and kidney injury as complications · 1+ blood is not a stone · catheter firstWhich process came first, and does it explain every other finding?

1Script2Urgent3Differential4Workup5Criteria6Severity7Treatment8Follow-upPractice
1Illness script
Bottom line
  • Months of hesitancy, weak stream and nocturia come first; retention, infection and a rising creatinine are its complications, not the cause
  • Acute retention: catheter first an alpha-1 blocker such as tamsulosin add a 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor for a large gland
  • A hard, nodular or asymmetric prostate, or a PSA (prostate-specific antigen) over 10, needs a biopsy
What it is

Nonmalignant overgrowth of the periurethral (transition zone) prostate with age; it does not raise cancer risk

Driver

DHT (dihydrotestosterone) drives the hyperplasia

Triggers

Age (non-modifiable)

For acute retention: anticholinergics (tricyclics, first-generation antihistamines), sympathomimetics, opioids, alcohol, anesthesia

An infection that swells the prostate

Chain

Narrowed urethra incomplete emptying stasis: infection and stones

Prolonged obstruction bilateral hydronephrosis postrenal kidney injury

Insights

Find the process that came first: the prostate explains the retention, the infection and the creatinine

1+ blood on a dipstick does not make it a stone HematuriaTrace to 1+ hematuria is expected with infection, a distended bladder and the vascular prostate itself; a stone needs colicky flank pain to the groin, and does not explain months of hesitancy.

2Urgent risks
RetentionNo urine, suprapubic pain, a distended bladder

If the bladder is full, choose a urethral catheter now; coudé tip if it will not pass, suprapubic if neither does.

Kidney injuryCreatinine rising behind the obstruction

If the creatinine is up, choose decompress, then renal ultrasound for hydronephrosis.

3Differential
Look-alikes, most tempting first
DiagnosisFingerprintDecides it
Benign prostatic hyperplasiaMonths of hesitancy, weak stream, nocturia, dribbling in an older manSmooth, firm, symmetric, nontender gland
Prostate cancerHard nodule, asymmetric enlargementPSA over 10 is worrisome; biopsy confirms
Drug-induced retentionRetention after a new anticholinergic, opioid or decongestantStop the drug
Acute prostatitisFever, dysuriaTender, boggy prostate
Kidney stoneHematuriaColicky flank pain to the groin
4Workup
Clues that change the answer
CluePoints toNext move
PSA mildly raised, smooth glandBPH can raise the PSARead it with the rectal exam
1+ blood on the dipstick after months of hesitancyExpected with infection, distension and BPHNot a stone without the colic
BPH with hypertensionOne drug for bothTerazosin
BPH with erectile dysfunctionOne drug for bothDaily tadalafil

Pause point. The bait: naming the retention, the infection or the creatinine as the cause, or reading 1+ blood as a stone. The six months of hesitancy came first, and the prostate explains every later finding.

5Diagnostic criteria
Defining criteria: BPH Symptoms – weak stream, hesitancy, nocturia, incomplete emptying · Exam – smooth, rubbery, symmetric enlargement · Exclude – infection, hematuria and cancer (urinalysis, PSA)
7Treatment
1

Every patientfrom diagnosis

Stop anticholinergics, sympathomimetics and opioids; treat any infection
2

Retentiona full bladder

Catheter first; suprapubic only if a urethral catheter fails
3

1st linebothersome symptoms

An alpha-1 blocker: tamsulosin, or terazosin if also hypertensive

Watch for orthostatic hypotension.

4

Addlarge gland

A 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor (finasteride); together they beat either alone

Shrinks the gland over 6 to 12 months; gynecomastia can follow.

5

Surgeryno response, or a complication

TURP (transurethral resection of the prostate)

For recurrent infection, stones, bladder damage or hydronephrosis; retrograde ejaculation is common after it.

8Follow-up
Follow-up decisions
WhenDo
Retention relieved by the catheterStart an alpha-1 blocker
Retention after a new anticholinergicStop it before adding drugs
Recurrent infections, stones or hydronephrosisRefer for surgery
Practice
  1. 72 yo M with 6 months of hesitancy, now anuric for a day with suprapubic fullness → Acute urinary retention from BPH → catheterize
  2. 72 yo M in retention; the question asks the underlying cause → Benign prostatic hyperplasia
  3. 72 yo M after catheter relief; first-line medical therapy → Alpha-blocker
  4. 72 yo M with a very large prostate seeking long-term volume reduction → Add a 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor
  5. 72 yo M with BPH started on oxybutynin for urgency, now in retention → Anticholinergic-induced retention → stop the drug
  6. 72 yo M in retention with a hard nodular prostate and prostate-specific antigen 40 → Prostate cancer → biopsy
The management sequel Acute retention → bladder catheterization first (suprapubic if the urethra is impassable). Then treat the UTI (urinary tract infection) and watch for post-obstructive diuresis. Expect the creatinine to fall; the fall proves the AKI (acute kidney injury) was post-renal. Renal ultrasound shows hydronephrosis if confirmation is needed. Long-term, give tamsulosin ± finasteride, with TURP (transurethral resection of the prostate) if refractory.
Transferable rule A single lab value should change the diagnosis only if it is incompatible with it, not merely compatible with another diagnosis.
